question: In MS Word, which option allows you to quickly remove all formatting from selected text while retaining the underlying text content?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Clear Formatting**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The "**Clear Formatting" **option allows you to **quickly remove all applied formatting** (like bold, italics, font size, color, etc.) from the selected text while preserving the actual text content.
 
• It can be found under the Home tab in the Font group, represented by an eraser icon labeled "Clear Formatting."
 
• You can also use the keyboard shortcut **Ctrl + Spacebar** to clear character formatting or **Ctrl + Q** to clear paragraph formatting.
 
• This feature is useful when you want to revert text to the default formatting without manually changing individual formatting elements.
 
• It removes custom formatting but retains the document's underlying style settings, such as the default **font and paragraph styles set for the document.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cut function in MS Word**

 
 
• The Cut function removes the selected text or object from its original location and places it in the clipboard, allowing you to paste it elsewhere in the document.
 
• You can quickly perform the Cut action using the keyboard shortcut** Ctrl + X**.
 
• The Cut option is typically used when you want to relocate content within the document or transfer it between documents.
 
 
 
• **Paste Special in MS Word**
 
 
• The Paste Special feature allows you to paste copied content in various formats, such as plain text, formatted text, or an image, depending on how you want the content to appear.
 
• You can access Paste Special by using the keyboard shortcut **Ctrl + Alt + V **or by selecting it from the Paste drop-down in the Home tab.
 
• It is useful when you need to control how content is pasted, for example, when you want to paste data as unformatted text or as a specific object, such as a picture or **HTML content.**
 
 
 
• **Format Painter in MS Word**
 
 
• Format Painter is a tool that allows you to copy formatting (such as font, color, size, and style) from one section of text and apply it to another, making formatting consistent across the document.
 
• It is located in the Home tab under the **Clipboard group,** represented by a **paintbrush icon.**
 
• You can use Format Painter by selecting the text with the desired formatting, clicking the **Format Painter icon**, and then selecting the text you want to apply the formatting to. **Double-clicking the icon** allows you to apply formatting to multiple sections.
